stories.title: Gibson Dunn Embraces Client Complexity With Breadth and Specialization
stories.excerpt: The real estate department at law firm Gibson Dunn has grown by 30 percent over the past two years, giving the group over 200 lawyers throughout 17 of the firm’s 23 offices worldwide, including in New York, Washington, D.C., Los Angeles, San Francisco and London, where the department has grown from six attorneys in 2021 to 21 today. This growth was organic, spurred by the client needs of a firm advising on some of the largest and most complex transactions in real estate. Recent examples include Blackstone’s acquisition of Safe Harbor Marinas, the largest marina and superyacht servicing business in the U.S., from Sun Communities for $5.65 billion in April 2025; Related Companies’ joint venture with Oxford Properties Group for the development of the 1.385 million-square-foot 70 Hudson Yards (which is going to be accounting giant Deloitte’s new U.S. headquarters); and RXR’s $540 million recapitalization of three New York City office towers collectively valued at over $3.5 billion. The firm also completed more than 225 data center transactions in 2025, including advising on a $16 billion joint venture between Blackstone and Related Digital. All told, the firm’s real estate department did $462 million in business in 2025, according to firm partner and department co-chair Jesse Sharf, who will celebrate his 40th year at Gibson Dunn in September. Sharf estimates that that number will rise to “well over $500 million” this year. Gibson Dunn’s real estate group — which, according to the firm, comprises over 10 percent of its total business — has long pursued expertise in the widest possible array of disciplines. “We do a lot of complicated transactions. bullets: Gibson Dunn real estate dept grew 30% in 2 years to 200+ lawyers across 17 offices

stories.summary: Gibson Dunn's real estate practice has grown 30 percent over two years to over 200 lawyers across 17 global offices, driven by demand for complex deal counsel. The firm's London office alone expanded from 6 to 21 attorneys since 2021. Recent mandates include Blackstone's $5.65B Safe Harbor Marinas acquisition, Related Companies' 1.385M SF development at 70 Hudson Yards (Deloitte HQ), and RXR's $540M office tower recapitalization, signaling robust capital flows into trophy real estate assets.
stories.impact: Strong institutional capital activity and complex transaction volume across office, mixed-use, and institutional real estate suggest stable debt and equity availability for large-scale development. Law firm headcount growth is a lagging indicator of robust deal flow; this signals favorable conditions for financing and closing major development projects in competitive markets like NYC, LA, and DC.

stories.title: Simon Raises 2026 Expectations as Leasing, Development Pipeline Accelerate
stories.excerpt: Simon Property Group’s second quarter offered more evidence that the nation’s largest mall owner is carrying its post-pandemic run into the second half of 2026. The real estate investment trust said Monday that its quarterly revenue, funds from operations (FFO) and tenant sales are all climbing while the company’s leaders raised its full-year outlook again. “Clearly, malls, retail centers at large are having a cultural moment,” CEO Eli Simon said. “People realize that they’re not going away. Young people want to hang out here.” The Indianapolis-based company generated $1.79 billion in second-quarter revenue, up 19.5 percent from $1.50 billion during the same period last year and 1.9 percent from $1.76 billion in the first quarter. Consolidated net income, meanwhile, reached $574.1 million, up about 1 percent from $568.5 million in the first quarter, but down 10.8 percent from $643.7 million a year earlier. Net income attributable to common stockholders was $483.1 million, or $1.49 per diluted share, compared with $556.1 million, or $1.70 per share, a year ago. (Last year’s second quarter included a noncash after-tax investment gain worth 21 cents per share.) Simon reported $1.18 billion in overall FFO, compared with $1.11 billion in the first quarter and $1.19 billion in the second quarter of 2025. Real estate FFO increased to $1.25 billion, up from $1.21 billion in the first quarter and $1.15 billion a year earlier. The performance prompted Simon to raise its outlook for the annual real estate FFO to between $13.20 and $13.30 per share, up by 8 cents. Leasing was particularly strong. Simon signed more than 1,200 leases encompassing more than 4.8 million square feet during the quarter, while the number of new deals increased more than 20 percent year-over-year. New leases accounted for about 28 percent of leases through the first half of the year, and initial base rents on new deals increased 17 percent from last year, while tenant allowances declined 12 percent. CEO Eli Simon cited a retail 'cultural moment,' noting that malls are not declining and young consumers actively seek in-person retail experiences.
stories.impact: Retail-anchored mixed-use development sentiment is strengthening; stronger retail health reduces default risk on retail-anchored multifamily projects and supports mixed-use underwriting assumptions in value-add and development scenarios. However, this is primarily a retail/retail REIT story with limited direct multifamily demand signal unless projects incorporate significant retail components.

stories.title: High Street Residential Tops Out on First Manhattan Development
stories.excerpt: High Street Residential (HSR), the residential subsidiary of Trammell Crow Company, has topped out construction on the firm’s first Manhattan project, The Marq, a 25-story luxury residential tower in SoHo. Slated for completion in the fourth quarter of 2027, the project will include 99 units, 2,072 square feet of ground-floor retail and 25 affordable apartments. Located on a vacant lot at 126 Lafayette St. in New York City’s Lower West Side, units at The Marq will range from studios to three-bedroom penthouses. “Our aim is for The Marq to reflect the vibrancy and elegance of this iconic community of SoHo,” said Michael Adamo, a principal with HSR in New York. “With its proximity to major transit hubs and green spaces like Hudson River Park, SoHo remains one of New York City’s most desirable locations for residential development. We’re proud to bring this project to life.” Along with its capital partners, other project partners on The Marq include Marvel Architects, general contractor Leeding Builders Group and interior designer Chris Shao Studio. stories.summary: High Street Residential, Trammell Crow's residential arm, reached topping-out on The Marq, a 25-story luxury residential tower in SoHo with 99 market-rate units and 25 affordable apartments, plus ground-floor retail. Located at 126 Lafayette Street in Lower Manhattan, the project is scheduled for completion in Q4 2027. Units range from studios to three-bedroom penthouses.
stories.impact: This marks TCR's flagship Manhattan luxury entry and signals confidence in SoHo/Lower West Side rental demand despite elevated construction costs and complex NYC regulatory environment. Delivery timing (Q4 2027) positions the asset for a competitive luxury market; the 25-unit affordable component signals compliance with NYC inclusionary zoning. Success here establishes HSR as a major player in trophy Manhattan multifamily and de-risks future development in constrained, high-barrier markets.

stories.title: Vietnamese Beauty Brand Hasaki Makes U.S. Debut in Cudahy
stories.excerpt: CBRE has arranged a 7,000‑square‑foot retail lease for Vietnamese beauty retailer Hasaki at Cudahy Plaza in Cudahy, marking the brand’s first U.S. store. Hai T. Dang with CBRE’s San Jose office represented the tenant. The landlord is Excel Realty Partners, LP. Cudahy Plaza, located at 7903–8017 South Atlantic Ave., is an open‑air retail center anchored by national retailers including Sprouts Farmers Market and Burlington. Founded in 2016, Hasaki is an omnichannel beauty and personal care retailer operating more than 300 stores, 18 clinics, and a nationwide e‑commerce platform in Vietnam. In addition to the Cudahy lease, CBRE represented Hasaki in a second 7,000-square-foot retail location at Magnolia Square, located at 1234 S. Magnolia Ave. in Anaheim, scheduled to open in the fourth quarter. “The center’s visibility, accessibility and heavy foot traffic aligned with Hasaki’s criteria for selecting a high‑performing location within Los Angeles County,” said Dang. Founded in 2016, Hasaki operates over 300 stores and 18 clinics in Vietnam. The company plans to open 10 additional U.S. stores, focusing on high-traffic centers in Los Angeles County.
stories.impact: International retail expansion into Southern California signals strong consumer demand and supports tenant mix diversification in mixed-use and retail-anchored projects. However, this is a tenant-placement story with no direct bearing on multifamily supply, demand, or capital markets.

stories.title: PE Firm OceanSound Expands Presence at SL Green’s 450 Park Ave.
stories.excerpt: SL Green Realty Corp said Monday that OceanSound, LP has signed a new five-year, 32,032 square foot lease covering floors 8, 22 and 23 at 450 Park Ave. The private equity firm, which focuses on the technology sector, currently subleases 21,640 square feet “We’re proud to extend and expand our valued relationship with OceanSound at 450 Park Ave.,” said Steven Durels, EVP, director of leasing and real property at SL Green. “The recent completion of various building upgrades has positioned 450 Park as the premier boutique office building for tenants seeking best-in-class workspace with upscale amenities at a luxury location.” OceanSound was represented by John Johnson of Savills, Inc. SL Green was represented by Paul Amrich, Neil King, Alex D’Amario, Matthew Dichter and Brooke Dewing of CBRE. Located at the southwest corner of Park Avenue and 57th Street, 450 Park is a 33-story office tower whose tenants include Banco Bradesco, Blue Crest Capital Management, Garnett Station Partners, Muzinich & Co, and Steadfast Financial. SL Green has completed building upgrades and is positioning 450 Park as a premium boutique office asset. Other tenants include Banco Bradesco, Blue Crest Capital, Garnett Station Partners, and Muzinich & Co.
stories.impact: Tech and PE sector office leasing in prime Manhattan locations signals continued demand for quality trophy office space, supporting SL Green's property values and refinancing capacity. However, this is an office asset story with no direct multifamily implications unless the building is part of a larger mixed-use development.

stories.title: MMCC Arranges Financing for Riverside County Self-Storage Property
stories.excerpt: Marcus & Millichap Capital Corporation (MMCC) arranged $7,380,000 in financing for Beaumont RV and Self Storage, a 49,958-square-foot self-storage property located at 251 W. 1st St. in Beaumont. Chad O’Connor, executive managing director in MMCC’s San Diego office, secured the 10-year financing with a national federal credit union on behalf of a private client. The loan carries a 5.75% interest rate and a 30-year amortization period. “Demand for self-storage remains supported by the sector’s durable operating fundamentals and the need for flexible space serving both household and recreational uses,” said O’Connor. “We were pleased to secure long-term financing with competitive terms that align with our client’s investment objectives.” Beaumont RV and Self Storage offers traditional self-storage units as well as dedicated RV and boat storage. The property is located near Interstate 10 and provides convenient access for customers throughout Beaumont and the surrounding Riverside County area. The post MMCC Arranges Financing for Riverside County Self-Storage Property appeared first on Connect CRE.

stories.summary: Marcus & Millichap Capital Corporation arranged $7.38 million in 10-year financing for Beaumont RV and Self Storage in Riverside County, California. The loan carries a 5.75 percent interest rate with a 30-year amortization period, provided by a national federal credit union. The 49,958 SF property offers traditional self-storage plus RV and boat storage near Interstate 10.
stories.impact: 5.75% fixed rate on self-storage debt signals modest tightening from peak lows but remains constructive for stabilized alternative real estate. Self-storage strength reflects population mobility and household formation; however, this sector does not compete directly with multifamily for land or capital in Riverside County's suburban market.

stories.title: 3650 Capital Furnishes Construction Loan for Yonkers Self-Storage
stories.excerpt: 3650 Capital has provided an approximately $24-million senior construction loan to finance the completion of 1060 Nepperhan Avenue, a 949-unit self-storage development located in Yonkers, NY. The project will be branded and operated by CubeSmart. The development is sponsored jointly by Cayre Equities and KCT Inc., the property’s original developer. The 3650 financing was provided as exit capital concurrent with the borrower’s emergence from a court-supervised reorganization. The transaction structure allows the sponsors to accelerate project completion while providing certainty to all stakeholders through an approved plan of reorganization.. The loan will be secured by a first-priority mortgage on the property and features a 36-month initial term with one six-month extension option. David Eyzenberg of Eyzenberg & Company served as the capital advisor structuring and arranging the requisite debt and equity. “This financing structure will enable the borrower to resolve all outstanding claims and facilitate the completion of a best-in-class self-storage facility in a supply-constrained market,” said Jonathan Roth, co-founder of 3650 Capital The post 3650 Capital Furnishes Construction Loan for Yonkers Self-Storage appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: 3650 Capital provided $24M senior construction loan for 1060 Nepperhan Ave., Yonkers, NY

stories.summary: 3650 Capital provided approximately $24 million in senior construction financing for 1060 Nepperhan Avenue, a 949-unit self-storage development in Yonkers, New York, to be branded and operated by CubeSmart. The project is sponsored jointly by Cayre Equities and KCT Inc. The loan features a 36-month initial term with one six-month extension option and is structured as exit capital from a court-supervised reorganization.
stories.impact: Large self-storage development in Westchester County signals durable demand for flexible storage; the use of a supply-constrained market narrative suggests tight self-storage availability. Yonkers is a secondary market with strong population density and transit access; self-storage supply constraints there could push residual demand to multifamily, but more likely indicates robust household formation and moving activity supporting multifamily demand indirectly.

stories.title: Law Firm Greenberg Traurig Takes 25K SF at Related Ross Dev in West Palm
stories.excerpt: Law firm Greenberg Traurig is relocating to another Related Ross building in Downtown West Palm Beach, Fla. The firm signed a 10-year lease to occupy about 25,000 square feet at the 15 CityPlace office development, which remains under construction, the tenant announced. The deal spans the entire 12th floor of the 25-story project. Move-in is scheduled for fall 2027. “The move reflects our long-term commitment to the West Palm Beach market and positions us to meet increasing client demand throughout Palm Beach County and beyond,” Tracy Gerber, co-managing shareholder of Greenberg Traurig’s West Palm Beach office, said in a statement. 15 CityPlace, and the neighboring 10 CityPlace, are expected to be completed next year after developer Related Ross secured a $772 million construction debt package last year. Health care provider Cleveland Clinic has already pre-leased 125,000 square feet at 15 CityPlace, which will span about 500,000 square feet. The law firm is currently stationed at Philips Point, where it leases roughly 30,000 square feet. Related Ross, led by Stephen Ross, purchased the 448,914-square-foot office for $282 million in 2021. The two-building complex, which dates back to 1985, is currently undergoing a $120 million renovation. Even as Greenberg Traurig departs, the building has nabbed new tenants: global index provider MSCI taking 7,500 square feet, investment bank Solomon Partners taking 4,200 square feet, and Integrity Pro Consulting taking 1,300 square feet. Julia Echikson can be reached at jechikson@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Greenberg Traurig leased 25,000 SF at Related Ross's 15 CityPlace, West Palm Beach, FL

stories.summary: Law firm Greenberg Traurig signed a 10-year lease for 25,000 square feet at Related Ross's 15 CityPlace, an under-construction 25-story office tower in Downtown West Palm Beach, Florida. The firm will occupy the entire 12th floor with move-in scheduled for fall 2027. Cleveland Clinic has pre-leased 125,000 SF at the project, which received a $772 million construction debt package and is expected to complete in 2027.
stories.impact: Strong anchor tenant (Cleveland Clinic) and professional services demand in West Palm Beach office market signals robust job growth and employer expansion in South Florida. Office and healthcare tenant pre-leasing supports mixed-use development viability in Downtown WPB; law firm relocation reflects confidence in the market's recovery and positions multifamily developers to capture incoming professional workforce demand in nearby residential markets.

stories.title: Law Firm Dunn Isaacson Rhee Leases 11K SF at 7 World Trade Center
stories.excerpt: Washington D.C.-based law firm Dunn Isaacson Rhee is establishing a new office in New York City. The firm, which specializes in high stakes trials, investigations and crisis management, has inked an 11,167-square-foot lease on the 34th floor of 7 World Trade Center, developer and landlord Silverstein Properties announced Monday. Silverstein did not disclose the length of the lease or the asking rent. However, a source close to the deal noted asking rents in the building range from $100 to $150 per square foot. “We are excited to welcome our teams and our clients into our new Manhattan office later this year,” Jeannie Rhee, managing partner of Dunn Isaacson Rhee, said in a statement. “7 World Trade Center offers the ideal combination of thoughtful design, functionality, and a premier location in the heart of the Financial District and a stone’s throw to the Southern District of New York courthouse.” Dunn Isaacson Rhee will relocate from 11 Park Place, also in the Financial District. It’s unclear when the firm will make the move. Dunn Isaacson Rhee did not immediately respond to Commercial Observer’s request for comment. Lisa Ann Pollakowski, Cory Gahr and Richard Plehn from Lee & Associates represented the tenant in the deal, while Silverstein was represented in-house by Keith A. Cody, Gordon Hough and Harlan Strader, as well as by CBRE’s MaryAnn Tighe. Lee & Associates did not immediately respond to CO’s request for comment. “Dunn Isaacson Rhee represents the caliber of organization that continues to define 7 World Trade Center as one of Downtown Manhattan’s premier office destinations,” Silverstein’s Cody said in a statement. “Today’s leading firms are seeking workplaces that reflect their brand, support their people and provide an exceptional experience for their clients. stories.title: Alliance for Downtown New York Inks 14K SF at 42 Broadway
stories.excerpt: Nonprofit group Alliance For Downtown New York has expanded its Lower Manhattan footprint to 42 Broadway. The Downtown Alliance, which manages the area’s business improvement district, secured a 14,420-square-foot lease at the Financial District tower, according to a recent CBRE office market report. The Downtown Alliance plans to relocate its operations division to the 22-story office building, a spokesperson for the nonprofit told CO. The nonprofit’s corporate headquarters remain housed roughly three blocks north at Silverstein Properties’ 120 Broadway. JLL’s John Wheeler and his team at JLL represented the tenant in the negotiations. A spokesperson for the team did not respond immediately to a request for comment. The lease terms were not disclosed, but office asking rents in Lower Manhattan averaged $61.91 per square foot in July, according to the CBRE report. A spokesperson for the landlord, Avi Schron‘s Cammeby’s International Group, confirmed the recent transaction to CO, adding that the space is still under construction. It was not immediately clear whether Cammeby’s International Group worked with any outside brokers. Cammeby’s 42 Broadway is located near the intersection of Broadway and Morris Street. Appellate service organization Office of the Appellate Defender relocated there in November, joining a tenant roster that includes office suite provider TKO Suites, chiropractor Prestige Health and Wellness, dental practice DDS Group and cafe Gregorys Coffee. Emily Davis can be reached at edavis@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Alliance For Downtown New York leased 14,420 SF at Cammeby's 42 Broadway, Lower Manhattan

stories.summary: Nonprofit organization Alliance For Downtown New York, which manages Lower Manhattan's business improvement district, secured a 14,420-square-foot lease at 42 Broadway in the Financial District. The organization is relocating its operations division to the building, while its corporate headquarters remain at 120 Broadway. Lower Manhattan office asking rents averaged $61.91 per square foot in July 2024.
stories.impact: Nonprofit tenant activity in Lower Manhattan reflects stabilization of the Financial District office market and continued institutional confidence in the submarket. However, this is a lower-income office lease with no direct correlation to multifamily demand or supply; it is not indicative of strong employment or wage growth driving residential demand.
